correctness.rationale: The completed [1/2] Radau stability function has coefficient -1/108 at degree five. A distance-five pair has zero lower matrix-power entries and a positive fifth generator power. This proves a strict negative leading entry for every positively weighted connected graph of diameter at least five; connected symmetric spectral calculus gives the eventual positive stationary projector. For path orders two through six, all 55 upper-triangular rational entries have been reconstructed from the current package with exact integers and positive denominators. All numerators for orders two through five, and every six-path numerator except the opposite endpoints, have nonnegative coefficients with a strictly positive term. The exceptional rational identity reduces to one quintic with exactly one positive root by Descartes and an exact rational isolating bracket. The one-vertex path is immediate. The verification program was replayed and the proof does not mistake finite checks for the arbitrary-size argument.

value.rationale: Graph heat-step nonnegativity is essential when a diffusion integrator is interpreted as a probabilistic transition. The theorem gives an all-graph, sharp geodesic obstruction: no step reduction prevents negative transition entries for positive-weight diameter-five networks, though every connected undirected network becomes strictly positive again at large steps. The minimal path realizing that obstruction has a complete algebraic admissible-step classification, including a nontrivial exact quintic and the identification of the only offending entry pair. This motivates the specific finite cutoff as a benchmark and supplies a structural mechanism rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
